findings.observedBehavior: Playfield owns loot generation, corpse inventory, credits and transfer orchestration.
findings.whyWeak: Policy, state, packets and lifecycle cannot evolve independently.
findings.failureMode: Every loot category adds branches to the playfield god object.
findings.recommendedCorrection: extract loot generation, corpse inventory and rights services

findings.observedBehavior: DB, debug, captured-profile and special outcome tables coexist with implicit precedence.
respawn ownership is type-specific and lacks shared camp timers or recovery.
findings.whyWeak: timers cannot be coordinated or cancelled uniformly.
findings.failureMode: duplicate/stale spawns and lost schedules on reset/restart
findings.futureScalingImpact: timer-per-spawn risk across hundreds of playfields
findings.recommendedCorrection: keyed global scheduler and population state

findings.observedBehavior: three materialization paths exist without spawn groups/controllers.
findings.whyWeak: placement, activation and lifecycle are coupled to source format.
findings.futureScalingImpact: cannot scale consistently to broad world coverage

findings.observedBehavior: no durable world population, camp, event or lockout state contract exists.
findings.failureMode: boss/camp/event state resets or becomes stale
findings.recommendedCorrection: versioned PopulationStateStore with explicit durable categories

findings.observedBehavior: 174 community-documented rows exist only as evidence.
findings.whyWeak: approximate levels/locations are not runtime proof.
findings.recommendedCorrection: inactive evidence-bearing camp proposals and capture review

findings.observedBehavior: candidate selection is bounded but selected packets are sent immediately without pacing.
findings.whyWeak: large dense clusters can burst queues.
findings.recommendedCorrection: measure budgets and add evidence-backed queue pacing if needed

findings.whyWeak: cost grows with all loaded characters.
findings.recommendedCorrection: use playfield/owner registries and guard hot paths

findings.observedBehavior: many useful guards are source assertions and aggregate validation has established failures.
findings.whyWeak: renames can break tests while semantic regressions can pass.
findings.failureMode: brittle feedback and hidden lifecycle regressions

findings.observedBehavior: large generated C# arrays coexist with DB and JSON loaders.
findings.failureMode: slow review, duplicate identities and divergent loaders

findings.observedBehavior: single-user captured flows are implemented; team/personal/concurrent semantics are absent.
findings.failureMode: duplication, denial or incorrect cleanup under multiple users
findings.recommendedCorrection: rights/access state machine; keep unknown packets blocked

findings.observedBehavior: scripted behavior is implemented by one-off handlers without a capability boundary.
findings.whyWeak: global behavior can migrate into boss modules.
findings.recommendedCorrection: narrow IEncounterModule and data-only boss guard
